Peters

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Subtype-specific plasticity of inhibitory circuits in motor cortex during motor learning

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how inhibitory interneuron subtypes regulate where and when excitatory synapses change during motor skill learning
span.quote: Motor skill learning induces long-lasting reorganization of dendritic spines, major sites of excitatory synapses, in the motor cortex. However, mechanisms that regulate these excitatory synaptic changes remain poorly understood.

span.label: how does the circuit know when and where to modify synapses to encode a new motor skill
span.quote: In other words, how does the circuit know when and where to modify synapses to encode a new motor skill?

span.label: shows learning-related spine reorganization is confined to the dendritic compartment that somatostatin interneurons inhibit, that those interneurons lose boutons as learning begins, and that both raising and lowering their activity impairs learning
span.quote: Our results identify SOM inhibition of distal dendrites as a key regulator of learning-related changes in excitatory synapses and the acquisition of motor skills.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Our results identify SOM inhibition of distal dendrites as a key regulator of learning-related changes in excitatory synapses and the acquisition of motor skills.

span.label: motor skill learning
span.quote: Motor skill learning induces long-lasting reorganization of dendritic spines, major sites of excitatory synapses, in the motor cortex.

span.label: in-vivo-two-photon-imaging
span.quote: In this study, we used in vivo two-photon imaging in awake mice to chronically monitor the dynamics of dendritic spines of excitatory neurons and axonal boutons of SOM-INs and PV-INs throughout motor learning.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Learning-driven loss of SOM-IN boutons reduces inhibition of distal dendrites, which depolarizes those dendrites and creates conditions favouring synaptic potentiation and the stabilization of new spines
span.quote: In light of these previous studies, we postulate that the reduced inhibition of distal dendrites by SOM-INs that we identify here during learning makes the local dendrites more depolarized, creating a condition that favors synaptic potentiation and the stabilization of learning-related spines.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The rise in PV-IN boutons acts as a homeostatic compensation for the loss of SOM inhibition and the consequent increase in excitatory-neuron excitability
span.quote: We speculate that this increase of PV-IN boutons is a homeostatic response to the learning-related reduction of SOM-IN inhibition and the resulting increase in the excitability of excitatory neurons.

span.label: the same variable is pushed in both directions and produces the same behavioural deficit, which is evidence for an optimum rather than for a direction of effect
span.quote: Optogenetic enhancement and suppression of SOM-IN activity during training destabilized and hyper-stabilized spines, respectively, and both manipulations impaired the learning of stereotyped movements.

span.label: the spatial logic is read off the anatomy: the compartment that changes is exactly the one the decreasing interneuron type targets, and the compartment that does not change is the one the increasing type targets
span.quote: Taken together, these results indicate that motor learning induces opposing changes in SOM- and PV-INs, with a reduction in the density of boutons made by distally-targeting SOM-INs and an increase in the density of boutons made by perisomatically-targeting PV-INs.

span.label: a confound is named and then measured directly rather than argued away - fewer SOM boutons need not mean less inhibition onto excitatory dendrites, so the inhibitory synapses themselves are imaged
span.quote: However, SOM-INs inhibit not only excitatory neurons but also other inhibitory neuron types 21 , and therefore the reduction in SOM boutons does not necessitate a reduction in inhibitory synapses onto excitatory neuron dendrites.

span.label: the specificity of the manipulation is established twice over: the same stimulation after learning does nothing, and the same protocol on a different interneuron type does nothing
span.quote: The observed effects of SOM-IN manipulation on spine dynamics and learning were in stark contrast to when PV-INs were activated using the same protocol, which neither affected spine dynamics nor behavior ( Supplementary Fig. 6b, d and e ), indicating that the impairment of learning-related spine dynamics and motor learning was specific to SOM-IN activation.

span.label: imaging three times a day separates the clocks of the two elements, showing the inhibitory change leads the excitatory one
span.quote: We found that the vast majority of spine changes occurred between 2 hours after training and the next day ( Fig. 2g ), consistent with a recent study 26 . PV bouton changes also followed a similar trend ( Fig. 4e ). However, about 50% of the changes in SOM boutons occurred during or within 2 hours after behavioral sessions ( Fig. 3e ), indicating that training induces a rapid elimination of SOM boutons.

span.label: an untrained-but-water-restricted control and an anatomically adjacent cortical area both serve as internal controls for the imaging itself
span.quote: We found that motor learning led to a significant reduction in the density of SOM boutons ( Fig. 3d ). However, bouton density was stable in the forelimb area of untrained mice and in the hindlimb area during training

span.label: retraining a month later shows no further reorganization, which localises the whole phenomenon to initial acquisition
span.quote: During this retraining, spines and SOM and PV boutons were stable ( Fig. 5d ), demonstrating that the reorganization of local synaptic circuits is specific to the initial acquisition of a new motor skill.

span.label: the optogenetic controls rule out the two trivial explanations separately - expression without light, and light without training
span.quote: Neither ChR2 expression alone without blue light stimulation nor ChR2 stimulation without training affected spine dynamics

span.label: sparse labelling by dilute Cre virus is what makes individual spines resolvable across eleven daily sessions
span.quote: To address this issue, we expressed GFP-tagged Gephyrin, a postsynaptic scaffolding protein at inhibitory synapses, in L2/3 excitatory neurons using in utero electroporation

span.label: the mechanism proposed is left explicitly as a postulate, tied to prior work on dendritic excitability rather than measured here
span.quote: In light of these previous studies, we postulate that the reduced inhibition of distal dendrites by SOM-INs that we identify here during learning makes the local dendrites more depolarized, creating a condition that favors synaptic potentiation and the stabilization of learning-related spines.

span.label: the opposite change in the other interneuron type is offered as speculation and labelled as such
span.quote: We speculate that this increase of PV-IN boutons is a homeostatic response to the learning-related reduction of SOM-IN inhibition and the resulting increase in the excitability of excitatory neurons.

span.label: The authors cannot rule out that circuit components other than SOM-INs also affect spine dynamics and learning.
span.quote: While we cannot claim that SOM-INs are the only circuit component whose manipulation affects spine dynamics and learning, these results support the unique role of SOM-INs in regulating learning-related plasticity in distal dendritic branches.

span.label: The scoring-correction rule may cause the reported spine/bouton dynamics to be underestimated.
span.quote: While this corrected for mistakes in scoring, we may be slightly underestimating the dynamics.

span.label: Sample sizes were not determined by statistical power calculation.
span.quote: No statistical tests were used to predetermine sample sizes but our sample sizes are similar to other previously reported studies 14 , 47 .

span.label: Normality of the data was assumed rather than tested.
span.quote: Data distribution was assumed to be normal in all experiments but this was not formally tested, and all statistical analyses were performed with Matlab.

span.label: other circuit components may also matter; only the sufficiency of this one is shown
span.quote: While we cannot claim that SOM-INs are the only circuit component whose manipulation affects spine dynamics and learning, these results support the unique role of SOM-INs in regulating learning-related plasticity in distal dendritic branches.

span.label: the proposed dendritic-excitability mechanism is a postulate built on other studies, not a measurement in this one
span.quote: In light of these previous studies, we postulate that the reduced inhibition of distal dendrites by SOM-INs that we identify here during learning makes the local dendrites more depolarized, creating a condition that favors synaptic potentiation and the stabilization of learning-related spines.

span.label: the homeostatic interpretation of the PV increase is explicitly speculative
span.quote: We speculate that this increase of PV-IN boutons is a homeostatic response to the learning-related reduction of SOM-IN inhibition and the resulting increase in the excitability of excitatory neurons.

span.label: manipulating interneurons could in principle perturb the circuit non-specifically, which the paper addresses with two controls rather than excluding outright
span.quote: Manipulation of the activity of inhibitory neurons could in theory non-specifically affect circuit activity and plasticity. However, two lines of evidence argue against this possibility.

span.label: two opsins with opposite sign in the same cell type, which is what makes a bidirectional test of an optimum possible at all
span.quote: Optogenetic enhancement and suppression of SOM-IN activity during training destabilized and hyper-stabilized spines, respectively, and both manipulations impaired the learning of stereotyped movements.

span.label: in utero electroporation, used to place a postsynaptic inhibitory marker in excitatory neurons so that inhibition onto them can be counted directly
span.quote: To address this issue, we expressed GFP-tagged Gephyrin, a postsynaptic scaffolding protein at inhibitory synapses, in L2/3 excitatory neurons using in utero electroporation

span.label: inhibition as a quantity with a direction of effect versus as a quantity with an optimal level - too much and too little are both detrimental, so neither sign describes it
span.quote: Our observations on the rapid loss of SOM-IN boutons and the bidirectional effects of SOM-IN inhibition on the spine stability observed in the optogenetic manipulations further demonstrate that spine stability on distal dendrites is exquisitely sensitive to the level of SOM-IN inhibition; too much or too little SOM inhibition is detrimental to spine reorganization and motor learning.

span.label: spine change - formation versus elimination; SOM activation blocked stabilisation of new spines while SOM inactivation abolished elimination of old ones, so the two are separately controlled
span.quote: In this condition, learning-related spine formation happened normally ( Fig. 7d-e , Supplementary Fig. 6d ) but spine elimination was almost completely abolished ( Fig. 7d, f-g ). This resulted in an increased spine density that was maintained until the end of training

span.label: plasticity - of the initial acquisition versus of the retained skill; a month later the same task produces no reorganization and the same manipulation produces no deficit
span.quote: Importantly, once the mice had acquired the skill, SOM-IN activation did not affect their performance ( Fig. 8e-f ). Thus, the effect of SOM-IN activation is specific to the acquisition of a new motor skill.

span.label: fewer SOM boutons versus less inhibition onto excitatory dendrites - not the same claim, because SOM cells also inhibit other interneurons
span.quote: However, SOM-INs inhibit not only excitatory neurons but also other inhibitory neuron types 21 , and therefore the reduction in SOM boutons does not necessitate a reduction in inhibitory synapses onto excitatory neuron dendrites.

span.label: inhibitory neuron as one class versus as genetically defined subtypes with distinct targets - the whole result depends on the second reading
span.quote: Different subtypes of inhibitory neurons target different domains of excitatory neurons, affording them the ability to control the spatiotemporal activity of excitatory neurons.

span.label: dendritic compartment - distal apical in L1 versus perisomatic in L2/3; the same neuron behaving differently in its two parts
span.quote: In contrast to the reorganization of distal spines, spines on perisomatic dendrites (<75 μm from soma) in L2/3 were relatively stable during learning

span.label: extends → previous studies showing that motor learning induces new dendritic spines in motor cortex which correlate with long-lasting motor memories (the paper's refs 1, 10, 31, 11)
span.quote: Here we extend these studies by investigating spine plasticity in different dendritic compartments as well as bouton plasticity of two genetically-defined inhibitory neuron types in the motor cortex during motor learning.

span.label: extends → previous studies showing inhibitory gating of excitatory plasticity (the paper's refs 13-20)
span.quote: The notion that subtype-specific inhibitory circuit plasticity regulates compartment-specific spine plasticity is an extension of previous studies showing inhibitory gating of excitatory plasticity 13 – 20 .

span.label: extends → studies showing motor learning establishes new spines in motor cortex, by asking what confines them to one compartment
span.quote: Motor skill learning induces long-lasting reorganization of dendritic spines, major sites of excitatory synapses, in the motor cortex. However, mechanisms that regulate these excitatory synaptic changes remain poorly understood.

span.label: builds-on → evidence that inhibition gates excitatory plasticity, including monocular-deprivation work in visual cortex
span.quote: Manipulation of the activity of inhibitory neurons could in theory non-specifically affect circuit activity and plasticity. However, two lines of evidence argue against this possibility.

span.label: supports → the finding that the level of GABAergic inhibition determines whether synapses depress or potentiate
span.quote: Furthermore, the level of GABAergic inhibition can control dendritic excitability and synaptic plasticity, with more and less inhibition favoring synaptic depression and potentiation, respectively

span.label: extends → work showing branch-specific dendritic calcium events are controlled by local inhibition
span.quote: In light of these previous studies, we postulate that the reduced inhibition of distal dendrites by SOM-INs that we identify here during learning makes the local dendrites more depolarized, creating a condition that favors synaptic potentiation and the stabilization of learning-related spines.

span.label: supports → reports that homeostatic changes in inhibition occur in PV but not SOM interneurons
span.quote: We speculate that this increase of PV-IN boutons is a homeostatic response to the learning-related reduction of SOM-IN inhibition and the resulting increase in the excitability of excitatory neurons.

span.label: SOM-INs —causes→ apical dendrites
span.quote: For example, somatostatin-expressing inhibitory neurons (SOM-INs) typically project their axons to the uppermost layer of cortex, L1, where they inhibit distal portions of apical dendrites of excitatory neurons.

span.label: PV-INs —causes→ perisomatic dendrites
span.quote: In contrast, parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory neurons (PV-INs) mainly target and inhibit somatic and perisomatic regions of excitatory neurons and regulate their spike output.

span.label: SOM-INs —contrasted-with→ PV-INs
span.quote: Taken together, these results indicate that motor learning induces opposing changes in SOM- and PV-INs, with a reduction in the density of boutons made by distally-targeting SOM-INs and an increase in the density of boutons made by perisomatically-targeting PV-INs.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · apical dendrites —contrasted-with→ perisomatic dendrites
span.quote: In contrast to the reorganization of distal spines, spines on perisomatic dendrites (<75 μm from soma) in L2/3 were relatively stable during learning

span.label: motor skill learning —causes→ dendritic spines
span.quote: Motor skill learning induces long-lasting reorganization of dendritic spines, major sites of excitatory synapses, in the motor cortex. However, mechanisms that regulate these excitatory synaptic changes remain poorly understood.

span.label: spine formation —distinct-from→ spine elimination
span.quote: In this condition, learning-related spine formation happened normally ( Fig. 7d-e , Supplementary Fig. 6d ) but spine elimination was almost completely abolished ( Fig. 7d, f-g ). This resulted in an increased spine density that was maintained until the end of training

span.label: motor skill learning —operationalised-as→ stereotyped movements
span.quote: Furthermore, their lever-press movements became more reproducible ( Fig. 1d ), shown by higher correlations of individual movements within and across later sessions

span.label: GABAergic —causes→ dendritic excitability
span.quote: Furthermore, the level of GABAergic inhibition can control dendritic excitability and synaptic plasticity, with more and less inhibition favoring synaptic depression and potentiation, respectively

span.label: apical dendrites —contrasted-with→ perisomatic dendrites
span.quote: Here using in vivo two-photon imaging in awake mice, we found that learning-induced spine reorganization of L2/3 excitatory neurons occurs in the distal branches of their apical dendrites in L1 but not in the perisomatic dendrites.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Statistical significance was determined by bootstrap test, one-way, or two-way ANOVA with post hoc corrections and two-tailed tests were used for all comparisons unless indicated.

span.label: bootstrap
span.quote: Statistical significance was determined by bootstrap test, one-way, or two-way ANOVA with post hoc corrections and two-tailed tests were used for all comparisons unless indicated.

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: All data points are presented as mean ± s.e.m except in supplementary Fig. 5a , data points are presented as median.

span.label: correlation
span.quote: Similarity of lever trajectories across trials was computed by Pearson correlation.

span.label: correlations of individual movements
span.quote: Furthermore, their lever-press movements became more reproducible ( Fig. 1d ), shown by higher correlations of individual movements within and across later sessions

span.label: bouton density
span.quote: We found that motor learning led to a significant reduction in the density of SOM boutons ( Fig. 3d ). However, bouton density was stable in the forelimb area of untrained mice and in the hindlimb area during training

span.label: puncta density
span.quote: By repeatedly imaging the same distal branches of apical dendrites in L1 ( Fig. 6b and Supplementary Fig. 1f ), we found that GFP-positive puncta density decreased during learning, compared to untrained control ( Fig. 6c ). The time course and extent of Gephyrin-GFP dynamics mirrored those of SOM boutons. Thus, inhibitory synapses on distal dendrites of excitatory neurons are reduced during motor learning.

span.label: Motor learning reorganized dendritic spines only on the distal apical dendrites of L2/3 excitatory neurons in layer 1, leaving perisomatic dendrites stable, i.e. the plasticity was confined to a specific dendritic compartment.
span.quote: Here using in vivo two-photon imaging in awake mice, we found that learning-induced spine reorganization of L2/3 excitatory neurons occurs in the distal branches of their apical dendrites in L1 but not in the perisomatic dendrites.

span.label: The two inhibitory neuron subtypes changed in opposite directions during training: SOM-IN boutons dropped early while PV-IN boutons rose gradually.
span.quote: Somatostatin-expressing inhibitory neurons (SOM-INs) that mainly inhibit distal dendrites of excitatory neurons showed a decrease in axonal boutons immediately after the training begins, whereas parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory neurons (PV-INs) that mainly inhibit perisomatic regions of excitatory neurons exhibited a gradual increase in the axonal boutons during training.

span.label: Both increasing and decreasing SOM-IN activity optogenetically disrupted spine dynamics and impaired the acquisition of stereotyped movements, so learning depends on an intermediate level of SOM inhibition.
span.quote: Optogenetic enhancement and suppression of SOM-IN activity during training destabilized and hyper-stabilized spines, respectively, and both manipulations impaired the learning of stereotyped movements.

span.label: Inhibitory postsynaptic sites on the distal dendrites of excitatory neurons, imaged as Gephyrin-GFP puncta, also declined during learning, confirming that the SOM bouton loss translates into less dendritic inhibition of excitatory cells.
span.quote: Thus, inhibitory synapses on distal dendrites of excitatory neurons are reduced during motor learning.

span.label: Activating SOM-INs did not block the formation of new spines but blocked their stabilization and additionally destabilized older spines.
span.quote: However, SOM-IN activation prevented the stabilization of these learning-related nascent spines and also destabilized some of the pre-existing spines

span.label: Silencing SOM-INs left spine formation intact while nearly eliminating spine loss, showing spine turnover is bidirectionally sensitive to SOM inhibition.
span.quote: Thus, spine dynamics is highly sensitive to the level of SOM inhibition.

span.label: The bouton changes were specific to trained forelimb cortex: untrained animals and the hindlimb area showed no change.
span.quote: However, bouton density was stable in the forelimb area of untrained mice and in the hindlimb area during training

span.label: Behaviourally, SOM-IN activation increased missed trials and prevented movement kinematics from becoming stereotyped.
span.quote: Furthermore, activation of SOM-INs blocked the formation of stereotyped movements, shown by the low trial-to-trial correlation of their movement kinematics throughout training

span.label: both raising and lowering SOM interneuron activity during training impaired learning of stereotyped movements
span.quote: Optogenetic enhancement and suppression of SOM-IN activity during training destabilized and hyper-stabilized spines, respectively, and both manipulations impaired the learning of stereotyped movements.

span.label: too much or too little SOM inhibition is detrimental to spine reorganization and motor learning
span.quote: Our observations on the rapid loss of SOM-IN boutons and the bidirectional effects of SOM-IN inhibition on the spine stability observed in the optogenetic manipulations further demonstrate that spine stability on distal dendrites is exquisitely sensitive to the level of SOM-IN inhibition; too much or too little SOM inhibition is detrimental to spine reorganization and motor learning.

span.label: spine formation rose in the distal apical branches in L1 during the first three sessions, followed by increased elimination of pre-existing spines
span.quote: In the distal branches of apical dendrites located in L1, spine formation was significantly increased during the first 3 sessions of training compared to untrained controls ( Fig. 2c-e ), followed by an increased elimination of spines that existed at the beginning of training

span.label: 75% of spines formed in the first three sessions survived to the end of the experiment
span.quote: 75% (18 out of 24) of the spines that formed in the first 3 sessions of training were stable and remained until the end of the experiment.

span.label: perisomatic spines stayed stable throughout learning
span.quote: In contrast to the reorganization of distal spines, spines on perisomatic dendrites (<75 μm from soma) in L2/3 were relatively stable during learning

span.label: SOM interneuron bouton density fell during learning, and was stable in untrained mice and in the hindlimb area
span.quote: We found that motor learning led to a significant reduction in the density of SOM boutons ( Fig. 3d ). However, bouton density was stable in the forelimb area of untrained mice and in the hindlimb area during training

span.label: PV interneuron boutons rose transiently instead
span.quote: In contrast to SOM-IN boutons, motor learning induced a transient increase in the PV-IN bouton density compared to untrained controls

span.label: inhibitory synapses on distal dendrites, measured directly by Gephyrin puncta, decreased during learning
span.quote: By repeatedly imaging the same distal branches of apical dendrites in L1 ( Fig. 6b and Supplementary Fig. 1f ), we found that GFP-positive puncta density decreased during learning, compared to untrained control ( Fig. 6c ). The time course and extent of Gephyrin-GFP dynamics mirrored those of SOM boutons. Thus, inhibitory synapses on distal dendrites of excitatory neurons are reduced during motor learning.

span.label: SOM activation left spine formation intact but prevented the new spines from stabilising, abolishing the density increase
span.quote: When ChR2 was activated in SOM-INs during training, a similar increase in spine formation rate was observed compared to control mice expressing tdTomato instead of ChR2 (sessions 1–3, Fig. 7d-e ). However, SOM-IN activation prevented the stabilization of these learning-related nascent spines and also destabilized some of the pre-existing spines ( Fig. 7f-g ). As a result, the increase in spine density was abolished with SOM-IN activation

span.label: SOM inactivation left formation normal but almost completely abolished elimination, raising spine density
span.quote: In this condition, learning-related spine formation happened normally ( Fig. 7d-e , Supplementary Fig. 6d ) but spine elimination was almost completely abolished ( Fig. 7d, f-g ). This resulted in an increased spine density that was maintained until the end of training

span.label: SOM activation made mice miss more trials, take longer to reach reward, and fail to form stereotyped movements
span.quote: Indeed, mice that had SOM-INs activated during training missed more trials than control mice ( Fig. 8b ) and took a significantly longer time to achieve the threshold for a reward from the cue onset ( Fig. 8c ). Furthermore, activation of SOM-INs blocked the formation of stereotyped movements, shown by the low trial-to-trial correlation of their movement kinematics throughout training

span.label: SOM inactivation impaired the same three measures
span.quote: Similarly, SOM-IN inactivation also impaired motor learning, shown by a lower fraction of successful trials, longer time to achieve a reward, and lower correlation of movement kinematics

span.label: the identical protocol applied to PV interneurons affected neither spines nor behaviour
span.quote: The observed effects of SOM-IN manipulation on spine dynamics and learning were in stark contrast to when PV-INs were activated using the same protocol, which neither affected spine dynamics nor behavior ( Supplementary Fig. 6b, d and e ), indicating that the impairment of learning-related spine dynamics and motor learning was specific to SOM-IN activation.

span.label: once the skill was acquired, SOM activation no longer affected performance
span.quote: Importantly, once the mice had acquired the skill, SOM-IN activation did not affect their performance ( Fig. 8e-f ). Thus, the effect of SOM-IN activation is specific to the acquisition of a new motor skill.

span.label: most spine changes occurred between two hours after training and the next day, while about half of SOM bouton changes occurred during or within two hours of the session
span.quote: We found that the vast majority of spine changes occurred between 2 hours after training and the next day ( Fig. 2g ), consistent with a recent study 26 . PV bouton changes also followed a similar trend ( Fig. 4e ). However, about 50% of the changes in SOM boutons occurred during or within 2 hours after behavioral sessions ( Fig. 3e ), indicating that training induces a rapid elimination of SOM boutons.

span.label: a month after training the skill was retained and no further spine or bouton reorganization occurred
span.quote: During this retraining, spines and SOM and PV boutons were stable ( Fig. 5d ), demonstrating that the reorganization of local synaptic circuits is specific to the initial acquisition of a new motor skill.

span.label: SOM and PV interneurons together make up about two thirds of cortical inhibitory neurons
span.quote: SOM-INs mainly inhibit distal dendrites of excitatory neurons, while PV-INs mainly inhibit perisomatic regions ( Fig. 3a ) 12 , and SOM- and PV-INs together compose about two thirds of cortical inhibitory neurons

span.label: pre-existing spines
span.quote: followed by an increased elimination of spines that existed at the beginning of training (‘pre-existing spines’, Fig. 2f )

span.label: Gephyrin
span.quote: we expressed GFP-tagged Gephyrin, a postsynaptic scaffolding protein at inhibitory synapses, in L2/3 excitatory neurons using in utero electroporation

span.label: successful lever-press
span.quote: A successful lever-press was defined as crossing of two thresholds (upper threshold ~0.5 mm, lower threshold ~1.5 mm in sessions 1 – 2, ~3.0 mm in sessions 3 – 4, and ~4.5 mm in sessions 5 – 11) within 200 msec.

span.label: movement bouts
span.quote: Movement bouts were identified as previously described 1 ; in brief, movement was detected by a velocity threshold, and the onset and offset of movement bouts were refined by the position of the lever respectively leaving or entering a stable state.

span.label: SOM-INs
span.quote: For example, somatostatin-expressing inhibitory neurons (SOM-INs) typically project their axons to the uppermost layer of cortex, L1, where they inhibit distal portions of apical dendrites of excitatory neurons.

span.label: PV-INs
span.quote: In contrast, parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory neurons (PV-INs) mainly target and inhibit somatic and perisomatic regions of excitatory neurons and regulate their spike output.

span.label: Gephyrin
span.quote: To address this issue, we expressed GFP-tagged Gephyrin, a postsynaptic scaffolding protein at inhibitory synapses, in L2/3 excitatory neurons using in utero electroporation

span.label: pre-existing spines
span.quote: In the distal branches of apical dendrites located in L1, spine formation was significantly increased during the first 3 sessions of training compared to untrained controls ( Fig. 2c-e ), followed by an increased elimination of spines that existed at the beginning of training

span.label: optogenetic activation (ChR2) or inactivation (eNpHR3.0) of SOM-INs during training
span.term: optogenetic activation (ChR2) or inactivation (eNpHR3.0) of SOM-INs during training
span.quote: To test whether the reduced SOM inhibition during learning is essential for spine reorganization, we used optogenetics to activate SOM-INs during learning

span.label: motor training on the cued lever-press task
span.term: motor training on the cued lever-press task
span.quote: In this task, mice under head-fixation learn to use their left forelimb to press the lever beyond the set threshold during an auditory cue to receive a water reward

span.label: density of dendritic spines, axonal boutons and Gephyrin puncta
span.term: density of dendritic spines, axonal boutons and Gephyrin puncta
span.quote: The total density of spines/boutons/puncta scored in each session was normalized to the initial session.

span.label: movement stereotypy (trial-to-trial correlation of lever kinematics)
span.term: movement stereotypy (trial-to-trial correlation of lever kinematics)
span.quote: Similarity of lever trajectories across trials was computed by Pearson correlation.

span.label: untrained mice and the hindlimb cortical area
span.term: untrained mice and the hindlimb cortical area
span.quote: However, bouton density was stable in the forelimb area of untrained mice and in the hindlimb area during training

span.label: tdTomato-injected littermates as opsin-free controls
span.quote: Control mice of the same genotype were injected with AAV2/1-CAG-FLEX-tdTomato (UPenn Vector Core).

span.label: spine formation
span.quote: In the distal branches of apical dendrites located in L1, spine formation was significantly increased during the first 3 sessions of training compared to untrained controls ( Fig. 2c-e ), followed by an increased elimination of spines that existed at the beginning of training

span.label: spine elimination
span.quote: In this condition, learning-related spine formation happened normally ( Fig. 7d-e , Supplementary Fig. 6d ) but spine elimination was almost completely abolished ( Fig. 7d, f-g ). This resulted in an increased spine density that was maintained until the end of training

span.label: bouton density
span.quote: In contrast to SOM-IN boutons, motor learning induced a transient increase in the PV-IN bouton density compared to untrained controls

span.label: movement kinematics
span.quote: Indeed, mice that had SOM-INs activated during training missed more trials than control mice ( Fig. 8b ) and took a significantly longer time to achieve the threshold for a reward from the cue onset ( Fig. 8c ). Furthermore, activation of SOM-INs blocked the formation of stereotyped movements, shown by the low trial-to-trial correlation of their movement kinematics throughout training

span.label: dendritic compartment
span.quote: In contrast to the reorganization of distal spines, spines on perisomatic dendrites (<75 μm from soma) in L2/3 were relatively stable during learning

span.label: 75% (18 out of 24) — proportion of spines formed in the first three training sessions that survived to the end of the experiment
span.quote: 75% (18 out of 24) of the spines that formed in the first 3 sessions of training were stable and remained until the end of the experiment.

span.label: about 50% — share of SOM bouton changes that happened during or within two hours of a training session, indicating rapid elimination
span.quote: However, about 50% of the changes in SOM boutons occurred during or within 2 hours after behavioral sessions

span.label: 6.7% ... (487 of 7215) — fraction of scored spines/boutons/puncta whose blind scoring was corrected, with 0.6% (45 of 7215) excluded outright
span.quote: In total, 6.7% of spines/boutons/puncta were corrected (487 of 7215), and only 0.6% were excluded (45 of 7215).

span.label: 11 sessions — length of the training protocol, one session per day, over which performance improved
span.quote: Mice showed a gradual improvement in performance with training over 11 sessions, one session per day

span.label: 11 sessions — training length, one session per day
span.quote: Mice showed a gradual improvement in performance with training over 11 sessions, one session per day ( Fig. 1b ), and the time from cue onset to achieving the reward significantly decreased over time

span.label: 75% (18 out of 24) — spines formed early that survived to the end
span.quote: 75% (18 out of 24) of the spines that formed in the first 3 sessions of training were stable and remained until the end of the experiment.

span.label: <75 μm from soma — the definition of perisomatic dendrites in this study
span.quote: In contrast to the reorganization of distal spines, spines on perisomatic dendrites (<75 μm from soma) in L2/3 were relatively stable during learning

span.label: about two thirds — share of cortical inhibitory neurons that are SOM or PV
span.quote: SOM-INs mainly inhibit distal dendrites of excitatory neurons, while PV-INs mainly inhibit perisomatic regions ( Fig. 3a ) 12 , and SOM- and PV-INs together compose about two thirds of cortical inhibitory neurons

span.label: one month — the retention interval after which the skill was retested
span.quote: Indeed, mice trained with the lever-press task maintained the skill one month after the original training, shown by high success rates and movement stereotypy

span.label: about 50% — SOM bouton changes occurring during or within two hours of a session
span.quote: We found that the vast majority of spine changes occurred between 2 hours after training and the next day ( Fig. 2g ), consistent with a recent study 26 . PV bouton changes also followed a similar trend ( Fig. 4e ). However, about 50% of the changes in SOM boutons occurred during or within 2 hours after behavioral sessions ( Fig. 3e ), indicating that training induces a rapid elimination of SOM boutons.
